title: I have done (present perfect) and I did (past)
subtitle: I have lost my key. / I lost my key last week.
summary: Use the past with a finished time (yesterday, last week) and the present perfect for a time that goes up to now.

lesson.heading: Finished time takes the past
lesson.text: With a *finished time* (**yesterday**, **last week**, **at 3 o'clock**, **in 2002**, **six months ago**) we use the past: **arrived / saw / was** etc. The time is over, so the sentence is over too.

lesson.heading: Do not use the present perfect with a finished time
lesson.text: Do *not* say **have arrived / have done / have been** with a finished time.

examples.text: We **didn't have** a holiday last year.
*A:* What **did** you **do** last night? *B:* I **stayed** at home.
William Shakespeare **lived** from 1564 to 1616. He **was** a writer. He **wrote** many plays and poems.

lesson.heading: When ... ? and What time ... ?
lesson.text: These questions ask about a finished time, so they always take the past.

examples.wrong: What time has Andy gone out

left.label: present perfect (I have done)
left.text: We think about now. No finished time is given.
examples: I **have lost** my key. (= I can't find it *now*)
Ben **has gone** home. (= he isn't here *now*)

right.label: past (I did)
right.text: We say when it happened. The time is finished.

left.label: time until now
left.text: The period goes up to now.
examples: **Have** you **ever been** to Spain? (= in your life, until now)
My friend is a writer. He **has written** many books.
We**'ve lived** in Singapore for six years. (= we live there now)

right.label: finished time
examples: We **lived** in Glasgow for six years, but now we live in Singapore.

lesson.text: If the sentence says *when*, use the past. If it only says *what has happened*, use the present perfect.

exercises.explanation: at 5 o'clock is a finished time, so we use the past: they arrived.

exercises.prompt: 'Have you started your new job?' 'Yes, ___ last week.'
exercises.explanation: last week is a finished time, so we use the past: I started it.

exercises.statement: I'm ready now. I've finished my work.
exercises.explanation: Correct. There is no finished time here - we are talking about now, so the present perfect is right.
Did you see Kate yesterday? yesterday is a finished time, so we use the past.
What time ... ? asks about a finished time, so we use the past.
yesterday afternoon is a finished time: I played.

exercises.prompt: Which tense goes with each time expression?

exercises.explanation: yesterday is a finished time, so we use the past: wasn't.

exercises.prompt: Kathy travels a lot. She ___ many countries.
exercises.explanation: No finished time is given - this is her life until now, so we use the present perfect.

exercises.prompt: You want to know if your friend has been to Florida at any time in their life. Write the question.
exercises.answer: Have you ever been to Florida?
exercises.explanation: ever means at any time until now, so we use the present perfect.

exercises.prompt: I live in New York now, but I ___ in Mexico for many years.
exercises.explanation: That period is finished - he lives in New York now - so we use the past: lived.

exercises.statement: Steve's grandmother has died two years ago.
exercises.explanation: Steve's grandmother died two years ago. two years ago is a finished time, so we use the past.
